reason: Both correctly explain E:15 as the anti-flood float being wet and tell the homeowner to isolate power and water. Conversation 1 is more informative, but it steers the homeowner into exactly the 'dry the tray, plug back in, run a cycle and watch' loop the situation warns against, suggests cutting the plinth sealant and unhooking an integrated unit themselves, and only makes the engineer conditional on recurrence. Conversation 2 is repetitive (asking twice about the sump) and overstates that there is 'no safe way' to remove the water, but it rules out the filter, declines to encourage reset-and-rerun, and lands on the correct, honest outcome: an internal leak that cannot be localised without pulling the unit, so book an engineer, with the leak source hedged rather than asserted.
